elements.element: Contractor must maintain commercial general liability insurance of at least USD 1 million per occurrence.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “comprehensive general liability insurance” with at least USD 1 million of coverage but does not state that the limit applies per occurrence.

elements.element: Contractor must maintain commercial general liability insurance with an aggregate limit of at least USD 2 million.
Contractor must maintain professional errors and omissions insurance of at least USD 2 million.
elements.evidence: The clause requires only USD 1 million of professional errors and omissions coverage.

elements.element: If Contractor processes Company data, Contractor must maintain cyber/privacy insurance of at least USD 5 million.
elements.evidence: The triggering condition is not demonstrably absent. The clause requires only USD 2 million of “cyber liability insurance” and does not expressly require privacy coverage.

elements.element: Contractor must maintain workers’ compensation insurance as required by law.
elements.evidence: The clause requires workers compensation insurance “in the amount required by statute” throughout the Agreement term.

elements.element: Contractor must provide certificates of insurance upon Company’s request.
elements.evidence: At Company’s request, Contractor must provide certificates or other acceptable evidence evidencing the required coverage.

elements.element: Contractor must maintain professional errors and omissions insurance of at least USD 1 million.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires professional errors and omissions insurance with coverage of at least USD 1 million.

elements.element: If Contractor processes Company data, Contractor must maintain cyber insurance of at least USD 2 million.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least USD 2 million of cyber liability insurance where Contractor processes or has access to Company data or Confidential Information, which includes the required processing trigger.

result.reason: The rendered clause reaches the fallback because it retains USD 1 million of E&O coverage and adds conditional USD 2 million cyber coverage. It does not reach the preferred position because the CGL limits are not stated as USD 1 million per occurrence and USD 2 million aggregate, E&O remains at USD 1 million, and cyber coverage remains at USD 2 million without express privacy coverage. The change is not minimal because the cyber obligation also applies based merely on access to Company data or Confidential Information, which is broader than the specified processing trigger. Existing commercial terms remain effective and no contradiction is introduced.
